lots.what_it_is: Two studio pottery figures signed McLAREN (incised): a horse-head bottle or whistle form with sgraffito spirals and a square-bodied owl, pale blue-green matt glaze. Style consistent with Gus McLaren (Melbourne studio potter, 1923-2014), not proven.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives. No sold, unsold or asking evidence for McLaren pottery was found; the three Gowans entries were other makers and are dropped. WebSearch budget was exhausted for me too, so Armitage past results, Invaluable and mainland houses could not be checked.
lots.working: No surviving SOLD evidence, so both maximums are 0.
lots.confidence_reason: Mark read clearly, but no matching sale of any kind; Gus McLaren attribution rests on style and surname only.
lots.dropped_entries: Dropped all three. Gowans 373963 '2 POTTERY OWL FIGURES' $130 hammer (listed 2025-11-10, API record opened, photo viewed by me): two unsigned painted terracotta-style garden owls, different maker and type, not comparable. Gowans 432501 'POTTERY HORSE FIGURES - SIGNED YEC' $380 (listed 2026-08-23, API record opened): different maker, contents unknown. Gowans 406972 'BOX OF SUNDRY ITEMS INC POTTERY OWL' $180 (listed 2026-05-03): mixed box, price not attributable. Records themselves are real and correctly priced, but none is the same item.
lots.key_photo_findings: Photo 3: incised 'McLAREN' signature on base of the horse figure, unglazed brown feet. Horse head is an open spout (bottle or whistle). A thin white band or cord is wrapped round the horse's neck in photos 1 and 2: could be decorative, or could hide a break and glue repair at the neck. Owl has incised square panel motif, no damage seen. Only the horse base is shown, so the owl's mark is unseen.
lots.condition: No chips seen in photos; neck band on the horse is unexplained and may conceal a repair. Owl base not shown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Is there a break or repair under the white band round the horse's neck? Is the owl also signed McLAREN on the base, and are there any chips to the ears, feet or spout?

lots.guide_summary: All sold hammers at Gowans for Littlewood estate-edition Lionel Lindsay prints, AUD, no rate needed. Range $20-140; the two cat images sold $90 and $140, other subjects mostly $20-35 with a few $45-100. One passed-in result. No asking evidence (WebSearch exhausted).
lots.working: Keep: closest same-series cat images sold $90 and $140 hammer at Gowans in the last 6 months. Using hammer as the price paid (conservative, it excludes Gowans premium): lowest $90 / 1.22 = $73.77, round down to $70. Flip: likely resale about $100 hammer at Gowans; less assumed seller commission and lot fee of about $20 (roughly 15% plus fee, assumed, not checked) and $0 postage (local room) = $80 / 2.44 = $32.8, round down to $30. Caution: no sale of this exact image was found, and non-cat images in the series sell for $20-35.
lots.confidence_reason: Publisher signature and 275/275 number read in photos; two close SOLD cat-subject entries opened with photos viewed, but neither is this exact image.
